nodes.label: Tiswell Concentric Arc Mark
nodes.rationale: The canonical vector source of the brand mark: four open, round-capped strokes of decreasing radius (72, 52, 33, 18) nested around a shared centre, each broken at a different angle so no ring closes. Built as pure stroked arcs with no fills and no text, so it scales to a 16px favicon and up to a 512px splash from one file. The innermost 18-radius arc is a half-circle read as a smile, turning the abstract nest of rings into a face at small sizes.

nodes.label: Tiswell Earth-Tone Palette
nodes.rationale: A four-step ramp — sage olive #9F9A77 outermost, tan #B6A284, warm brown #A2886E, dark brown #5E4634 innermost — over a cream field. The ramp darkens monotonically inward, so the innermost arc carries the most contrast and the eye lands on it first; that is what makes the smile legible at 192px where the outer rings blur into texture. Muted, low-saturation earth tones instead of a saturated brand hue keep the mark from competing with content.

nodes.label: Smile Arc Motif
nodes.rationale: The innermost path is the only arc drawn as an explicit open half-circle with sweep-flag 1 rather than a broken ring, and it is the heaviest stroke at 7.5 on the smallest radius. This is the payoff of the whole composition: at icon sizes the three outer rings read as an abstract nest, and the single dark curve at the centre resolves them into a face. It is also the one element the design cannot afford to lose to a maskable crop.

nodes.label: Centred Scale Transform Crop
nodes.rationale: The whole group is wrapped in translate(140 140) scale(1.7373) translate(-140 -140), a scale about the artwork centre rather than the origin. The arcs were authored on a 280 canvas at their natural radii and then blown up 1.74x in place, deliberately pushing the outer sage ring past the viewBox edge so it bleeds off. Keeping the magnification as a transform instead of rewriting every path radius means the arc geometry stays editable in the units it was designed in.
